name: Matrix
line: The cover is the real adjacency matrix of the Cancer Evidence Explorer, 185 exposure rows by 68 cancer columns, a filled red square for each established link and an outlined one for each suspected link; a lens opens the rows under the pointer like a loupe on a ledger and names them in the margin, a crosshair names each pair, and the signature moment is the scroll-driven Bertin reordering (A to Z, by kind and organ, by certainty, by reach) that ends on Tobacco smoking and Processed meat for the lesson.
notes: Two greys were added for text contrast (#4A4A4A body, #6E6E6E small labels); #8C8C8C is kept for non-text marks. On desktop rows are exposures and columns cancers, as directed; 185 rows cannot all be read at once, so rows are about 3 px and open up under the pointer (and around any selection) with their names in the right margin. Below 560 px the ledger turns on its side (exposures across, cancer types down) inside its own sideways-scrolling frame, so every square stays tappable and every exposure name stays legible; the captions and legend are worded to fit either orientation. Clicking a square or a row name opens that exposure, clicking a column name opens that cancer type. The two plates in the explorers section are small matrices drawn from graph.json and chronic-graph.json (the chronic file is used for drawing only). Geist and Geist Mono both include Cyrillic. Without JavaScript the explorers' network drawing stands in and all story text is shown in sequence.
